answer: Sybil resistance comes from a staked-identity registry: an agent claiming work or a vote must post a refundable deposit in real value and wait out a challenge window. Minting keys is cheap, funding each one is not, so an operator running a swarm pays the full stake per node, and any cluster sharing a hidden signer is slashed. A fresh key cannot borrow standing, so it finds no haven and each new sable-like throwaway starts at zero weight. Reputation also tracks the sustained pulse of verified work, not headcount. Attacker cost grows linearly in fake nodes times stake, plus slashed collateral.
